newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: The Spanish debt market dived on Monday, adjusting its level to last week's fall in major European markets and in U.S. Treasuries, when the bonos market was shut for the Easter holidays, dealers said.
"It was a boring day. We arrived this morning discovering the sharp fall in foreign markets. But that was all," a trader with a foreign house in Madrid said.
Low trading volume magnified the fall. The upcoming monthly Treasury refunding was also adding pressure.
"We also had a technical reaction. But it's good news the future ended above support at 111.52," a chart analyst said.
The Spanish Treasury will offer three- and 10-year bonds on Tuesday, and dealers said it was likely yields would be higher than one month ago.
"It's likely the Treasury will have to pay a premium over the secondary market," a dealer said.
But longer term the outlook remained midly positive.
"I expect interest to be back soon in maturities from three to five years," a dealer said.
"A moderate interest rate cut is possible within the next quarter if, as expected, inflation slips toward two percent May or June," wrote Salomon Brother in a note to clients.
